mcat_description.short: Prefab Steel Bunk House is a factory-manufactured, mild steel-framed portable accommodation unit designed for rapid on-site deployment, sold as a complete unit or in panel-based modules. Commonly used as worker sleeping quarters and labour colony housing at construction sites, industrial projects, and remote worksites across India.
mcat_description.long: Prefab Steel Bunk Houses are pre-engineered, modular structures built on a mild steel (MS) frame with panel-based walls — typically PUF, EPS sandwich panels, or GI sheet — and are manufactured off-site before being transported and assembled at the project location. Standard configurations range from compact single-room units (20×10×8.5 ft) to larger multi-room blocks (40×10×8.5 ft), with customisable dimensions, insulation grades, door/window counts, and interior fittings. These structures serve as temporary to semi-permanent accommodation for construction labourers, industrial workers, mining camp residents, and disaster relief personnel, offering weather resistance, portability, and significantly faster deployment than conventional construction. Key structural materials include mild steel sections for the frame, colour-coated GI or Galvalume roofing sheets, vinyl or FRP flooring, and aluminium sliding windows, with optional amenities such as electrical fittings, air conditioning, and attached toilet blocks.

market_context: Prefab Steel Bunk Houses in India are primarily mild steel-framed portable accommodation structures manufactured off-site and deployed at construction sites, labour colonies, mining camps, and industrial worksites. The dominant construction method uses MS sections for the structural frame with infill wall panels — PUF (polyurethane foam), EPS sandwich panels, or GI sheet — and colour-coated GI or Galvalume roofing. Standard commercial footprints are 20×10×8.5 ft and 40×10×8.5 ft, with double-decker and multi-module configurations available for higher-density labour colonies. The product is sold both as a complete ready-to-use unit (per piece) and on a per-sq-ft basis for custom dimensions. Key buyer vocabulary includes 'MS bunk house', 'portable bunk house', 'labour accommodation cabin', and 'porta cabin bunkhouse'. A notable premium sub-segment exists for rooftop prefab installations (e.g., Tata Nestin), though this is a small fraction of overall demand. Manufacturers are concentrated in Gujarat (Ahmedabad, Bhavnagar), Maharashtra (Pune, Mumbai), Karnataka (Bengaluru), and Delhi-NCR. The category overlaps with 'Porta Cabin' and 'Prefabricated Labour Colony' in buyer vocabulary — buyers searching for site accommodation may use these terms interchangeably.
